key_insight: Using memory manipulation—specifically experience replay—together with data augmentation in a Mamba-based language model yields markedly improved sample-efficiency for generating property-optimized small molecules.
problem_solved: Generative molecular design typically requires large amounts of data or many costly evaluations; this work addresses how to design high-quality molecules with far fewer training samples/evaluations.
method: Train a Mamba-based language model for molecular generation tailored to small molecules.
Apply targeted data augmentation to expand effective training diversity without extra experiments.
Use experience replay / memory manipulation: store and replay high-quality past samples to guide learning and improve sample efficiency.
impact: Reduces the data and evaluation budget needed for property-driven molecule design, enabling faster iteration and lower-cost discovery workflows for AI/ML practitioners in chemistry and drug discovery.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Mamba LM → data augmentation → replay buffer → generation loop (highlight memory replay path).
Bar or line chart: property score vs. number of samples showing improved sample-efficiency with replay+augmentation.
Icon set: molecule structures, memory/buffer icon, and a lightning/clock icon to represent speed/resource savings.
Example molecule before/after optimization to show qualitative improvement in target property.
paper_title: Sample-efficient generative molecular design using memory manipulation
paper_authors: Jeff Guo, Junwu Chen, Anthony GX-Chen, Philippe Schwaller
